caption: Jean Steinberg, Donor v. Commissioner
tax_type: gift (net gift with assumed sec. 2035(b) estate tax)

source.document_title: T.C. OPINION, JUDGE KERRIGAN 145 T.C. NO. 7 (DECISION WILL BE ENTERED FOR PETITIONER)

related: Steinberg v. Commissioner, 141 T.C. No. 8 (2013) (summary judgment, 'Steinberg I'; separate DAWSON docket entry 7fd46e10-ee5d-4a27-ad43-cb253ea917ed)

found_facts.snippet: increasing petitioner's gift tax liability by $1,804,908 for tax year 2007.
The fair market value of the properties transferred ... before consideration of the gift tax liability and section 2035(b) estate tax liability assumed by the daughters was $109,449,307.
the daughters each transferred $10 million to an escrow fund ... Of the $40 million, $32,437,261 was used to pay the Federal gift tax
petitioner reported taxable gifts of $71,598,056 and total gift tax of $32,034,311.

increased the aggregate value of petitioner's net gifts to her daughters from $71,598,056 to $75,608,963, for a total gift tax increase of $1,804,908 ... increased the value of petitioner's total gifts for tax year 2007 by $4,010,907 ... petitioner's entire $5,838,540 discount
The report calculated the gift tax liability to be $32,012,711.

issue: Whether the donees' assumption of potential sec. 2035(b) estate tax reduces the value of the net gift, and by how much.
holding: Yes; reduction of $5,838,540 (petitioner's unrebutted expert: IRS mortality tables + sec. 7520 rate). Decision for petitioner.

steps: Holding: discount allowed -> net gift 71,598,056 -> deficiency 0
non_reconciling: Notice increased the gift by 4,010,907, not the full 5,838,540 discount (fn. 2; parties nonetheless treat it as disallowing the entire discount).

Reported gift tax 32,034,311 vs expert 32,012,711 vs escrow-paid 32,437,261 (before credits) differ; prior gifts/credits are not stated, so the circular net-gift solve (Rev. Rul. 75-72) cannot be reproduced exactly.

judgment: value of sec. 2035(b) assumption ($5,838,540, actuarial expert)

caveats: The main amount at issue is a valuation; the arithmetic around it is exact.
